title: Evening tide deploy lab scratchpad
content:
Context and goal:
- Quick personal scratchpad for an evening, low-traffic canary intended to test model flip and a conservative pin-back strategy.
- Goal: validate new quantized variant (v2-q4) on production traffic without impacting SLA more than short blips; verify latency tail, memory footprint, and cache/kv warm behavior.
- Why evening: traffic floor, predictable client cohorts (background jobs + low-intent interactive), easier rollback window.

High-level plan (two-phase):
1) smoke cohort (0.2% of traffic, 10min baseline + 20min observation)
   - only run inference for cohort ids: internal-test, bg-jobs, pilot-client-A
   - health checks: 95th latency, error-rate, OOMs, GPU memory pressure, kv cache miss rate
   - manual watch: streaming time-to-first-token regression, function-calls correctness on sample set
2) slow ramp (0.2 -> 5% over 45min)
   - incremental jumps: 0.2 -> 0.5 -> 1 -> 2 -> 5 (each step 10m steady + 5m observation); back out on trigger
   - automated thermostat enforcer: if 95th latency > 2x baseline or error-rate > 0.5% for 5min, auto-pin to previous model and halt ramp

Instrumentation to verify before flip:
- Dashboards to have quick links: per-route 95/99, per-model token cost, GPU mem by host, kv hit ratio by prefix
- Ensure tracing: request -> model selection -> kernel version -> host id included in span
- Pre-load KV prefixes for high-volume prefixes from last 24h (script: tools/prewarm-prefixes.sh)
- Ensure continuous batching config on new variant is compatible (batch size max lowered to 64 to avoid OOM)

Commands / runbook snippets (to copy when doing the run):
- enable canary route: infractl route update --route=generate-v2-canary --weight=0.002 --model=v2-q4 --note="evening-tide-smoke"
- pin-back (fast): infractl model pin --route=generate-v2-canary --model=v2-1.12.4 --reason="auto-rollback"
- emergency full cut: infractl route update --route=generate --weight=1.0 --model=v2-1.12.4 --force

Rollback / alarm triggers (front-of-mind thresholds):
- latency: 95th > 2x baseline for 5 continuous minutes
- errors: 5xx or inference errors > 0.5% absolute increase vs baseline over 3 min window
- memory: any host reports GPU mem usage > 92% or OOMs logged -> immediate 0.2% pin back
- correctness: function-calling or structured output regression on canary testset (see list below)
- burst traffic + slow tail: if queue-depth grows > 1000 tokens across hosts for 10+ min -> rollback

Sanity check / probe scenarios (local testcases to run before enabling smoke):
- ticketed prompts: edge-case prompts (very long context; sparse token distribution) from INF-1987
- streaming probe: stream-100-reqs.sh against canary route, measure ttfb and total latency
- KV precond: run kv-smoke against top 50 prefixes, assert hit rate > 70% within first 5min

Quality watchlist (manual):
- hallucination/regression testset (50 golden prompts) — compare BLEU-like / edit-distance heuristics; human spot-check if threshold exceeded
- model output size: token inflation (>+15% tokens produced) can be costly and signal prompt handling regressions

Open questions / unknowns to decide before final run:
- Should we pre-warm the kv cache across all hosts or only subset? Pre-warm costs $$ but reduces early-latency noise. Lean: pre-warm warm-nodes only (10 hosts).
- Canary cohort composition — include a small percentage (0.05%) of mobile IDE telemetry? Pros: surface SDK regressions; Cons: user-visible. I tentatively exclude mobile.
- Autoscaler headroom: do we temporarily reserve a tiny burst pool during the evening window? If not, we risk spiky tail and delayed warm. Action: ping infra team (Marco) to confirm pool availability.

Checklist (quick, actionable):
- [ ] Confirm infra burst pool available (Marco)
- [ ] Upload canary golden set to S3 path: s3://playground/release-canary/2026-02-evening
- [ ] Prewarm KV prefixes (script run + baseline snapshot)
- [ ] Load tracing and dashboard links in side-by-side tabs
- [ ] Notify on-call (pager): Priya (eng-sre)
- [ ] Slack channel: #deploy-evening-tide (set to announcement + ephemeral updates)
- [ ] Run local stream probe and record baseline (attach results)
- [ ] Start smoke cohort (0.2%) and timestamp T0
- [ ] After smoke, take snapshot: latency, errors, kv-hit, mem
- [ ] If green, execute slow ramp (record each step)
- [ ] Postmortem stub: open INF-xxxxx and populate with timeline + links

Notes to self / heuristics learned from past runs:
- When we saw a late-tail problem (Jan run), it was tied to cold KV entries on a subset of hosts; pre-warming only the head nodes mitigated the spike.
- Lowering continuous batch max for the quantized build prevented sporadic OOMs at 2% traffic.
- Prefer manual gate at 1% (pause + thumbs-up) for model variants with nontrivial changes in tokenization or function-calling semantics.

Quick results template to paste into post-run notes:
- T0 (smoke start): <timestamp>
- smoke duration: <mins>
- smoke verdict: pass|fail + brief reason
- ramp events: list per-step timestamps + decisions (continue/pin/rollback)
- anomalies: host ids, stack traces, example failed request ids, golden-test diffs

Attachments and local artifacts (where I'll stash logs):
- /tmp/evening-tide-<date>-trace.jsonl (traces for smoke and first ramp step)
- s3://playground/release-canary/2026-02-evening/metrics-dump
- link to PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/842

Post-run analysis questions to resolve (if we hit regressions):
- Is regression coming from kernel selection change or quantization artifact? (A/B kernel logs to inspect)
- Did batching behavior diverge for short sequences? (check batch size histograms)
- If memory spike: was it due to cache duplication on small pool? (compare host allocation graphs)

Final note: Keep conservative mindset — evening windows are not fire-and-forget despite low traffic. This scratchpad is my step-by-step plan; will convert to a short team checklist after a dry run passes.

Unpolished TODOs (for me):
- write a tiny rollback script that automates pin + notify (make idempotent)
- add a test to infra-runbook that simulates KV cold start + small-batch OOM
- follow up with SRE on autoscaler policies and burst pool cost

End of scratchpad.
